properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1/ECDSA implementation shipped in this build: k256 is declared as a workspace dependency (root Cargo.toml:466 `k256 = "0.13"`), used first-party for the Tempo deposit ECIES ephemeral keypair (crates/cast/src/cmd/tempo/zone/encryption.rs) and transitively by alloy's Ethereum signers throughout anvil/cast/forge. Deadline risk under Shor; signatures migrate to ML-DSA-65, the ECDH half of k256's use to ML-KEM-768. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256r1 (P-256) in the EVM tooling, three surfaces: (1) vm.signP256/publicKeyP256 cheatcodes (docs in cheatcodes.json:9621/11565, implementation via p256::NistP256 in crypto.rs:602/:769); (2) the RIP-7212 P256VERIFY precompile support/gas constants in crates/evm/networks (lib.rs:29/1073); (3) the tempo keychain signature surface — anvil's backend constructs P256SignatureWithPreHash and WebAuthn (ES256 over P-256) keychain signatures at mem/mod.rs:947/:978 for AA transactions and gas estimation

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: ring 0.17.14 provides X25519 (and AES/ChaCha/SHA/P-256) to the build, typically via the TLS stack (rustls). X25519 is harvest-now-decrypt-later vulnerable under Shor; migrating means hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768 in the TLS layer once the rustls/ring versions support it. Observable here, replaceable only via dependency upgrades.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.17.14 enters via rustls's `ring` feature (crates/cli/Cargo.toml:63) and is force-installed process-wide as the rustls crypto provider (crates/cli/src/utils/mod.rs:263), so ring's Ed25519/X25519/AES-GCM/SHA-2 primitives back every TLS session the CLIs open. ring 0.17 offers classical groups only — no PQ hybrid. Changeable here by switching the provider.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: curve25519-dalek 5.0.0 is pulled transitively by commonware-cryptography 2026.9.0 (tempoxyz/tempo git stack, rev 6ef1f812) which the Tempo integration depends on; no first-party call site found in foundry code. X25519 key agreement is retroactively breakable (harvest now, decrypt later) wherever the Tempo chain stack uses it; ML-KEM-768 or X25519MLKEM768 hybrid replaces it. Observable here, replaceable only by the tempoxyz vendor.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Build-stage network fetch: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2` downloading cargo-binstall inside the rust:1.98-bookworm builder. A real TLS version floor on a real session (curl treats --tlsv1.2 as minimum); the fetch negotiates TLS 1.2/1.3 with Debian's OpenSSL 3.0 — classical ECDHE, no PQ groups. Transient build-time concern, changeable here, not application runtime crypto.

Graded at the AES-128 floor by the collector but the call sites resolve to Aes256Gcm (256-bit). Same chain as ALG-12f61078; kept separate as the mode/AEAD primitive view.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF-SHA256 deriving the AES-256-GCM deposit key in the tempo zone ECIES: production KDF at encryption.rs:47 takes the secp256k1 ECDH shared x-coordinate as IKM with public salt b"ecies-aes-key" and info binding portal/key-index/ephemeral-x/sender (context binding); :103/:116 are the test-side derivations; Cargo.toml:74 is the hkdf crate declaration. The b"ecies-aes-key" literal is a public ECIES domain-separation label, not secret material.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hmac 0.12.1 enters via eth-keystore 0.5.0 (Ethereum Web3 Secret Storage keystore encryption) alongside pbkdf2/scrypt/aes-ctr/sha2/sha3. HMAC is quantum-safe (Grover square-root only); recorded as dependency inventory. Changeable here only by changing the keystore implementation upstream of foundry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Key-management infrastructure (class 7): cast wallet sessions resolve remote signers from AWS KMS / GCP Cloud KMS / Turnkey environment credentials; this code strips those credentials from the session child so it can only sign with the injected session key. The keys and their algorithms live in the cloud KMS control plane — observable here, replaceable only by the vendor. Recorded because the tooling's signing posture depends on which algorithms those KMS accounts support.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ring 0.17.14 is the process-wide TLS crypto provider for every foundry CLI: crates/cli/Cargo.toml:63 enables rustls's `ring` feature and crates/cli/src/utils/mod.rs:263 force-installs `rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider()`, which backs all reqwest/tokio-tungstenite TLS sessions in forge/cast/anvil/chisel. ring 0.17 offers classical key exchange only (X25519, P-256/384) — choosing it forecloses rustls's X25519MLKEM768 hybrid until the aws-lc-rs provider is used. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: aes-gcm 0.10 is declared in crates/cast/Cargo.toml:73 and used first-party in the Tempo deposit ECIES: crates/cast/src/cmd/tempo/zone/encryption.rs:54 `Aes256Gcm::new((&key).into()).encrypt(...)` seals the deposit recipient/memo under an HKDF-SHA256 key. AES-256-GCM is quantum-safe; the scheme's quantum exposure is the secp256k1 ECDH that derives the key. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: rustls 0.23.45 is the workspace TLS stack: root Cargo.toml:483, reqwest 0.13 built with the `rustls` feature (:478), and the CLI installs the ring provider process-wide (crates/cli/src/utils/mod.rs:263). rustls 0.23 supports the PQ hybrid X25519MLKEM768 only under the aws-lc-rs provider; the forced ring provider means every TLS session the CLIs open is classical-only — harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure for RPC/etherscan/wallet traffic. Changeable here (provider + group config).

Quantum-safe. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context

Harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure on all CLI TLS traffic (RPC endpoints, Etherscan, wallet.tempo.xyz). Changeable here.
